arxiv-2002-04374.title: Convolutional Neural Networks and a Transfer Learning Strategy to Classify Parkinson’s Disease from Speech in Three Different Languages
arxiv-2002-04374.creator: J. C. Vásquez-Correa 1,2, T. Arias-Vergara 1,2,3, C. D. Rios-Urrego 2, M. Schuster 3, J. Rusz 4, J. R. Orozco-Arroyave 1,2, E. Nöth 1
arxiv-2002-04374.description: Abstract Parkinson’s disease patients develop different speech impairments that affect their communication capabilities. The automatic assessment of the speech of the patients allows the development of computer aided tools to support the diagnosis and the evaluation of the disease severity. This paper introduces a methodology to classify Parkinson’s disease from speech in three different languages: Spanish, German, and Czech.

arxiv-2406-17907.description: Abstract This paper addresses the computation of Delta-V-optimal, safe, relative orbit reconfigurations for satellite formations in a centralized fashion. This study aims to bridge the gap by addressing issues regarding textual information loss in surgical lecture videos and the spatial-temporal challenges of surgical VLP.

pmc-13181887.description: BackgroundChronic liver disease is often associated with vitamin D deficiency. (2) Appropriate congressional committees The term “appropriate congressional committees” has the meaning given that term.

uslaw-usc-t31-s3301.title: 31 U.S.C. § 3301 — General duties of the Secretary of the Treasury
uslaw-usc-t31-s3301.creator: United States Congress
uslaw-usc-t31-s3301.description: United States Code, Title 31 (Money And Finance); Chapter 33 (Depositing, Keeping, And Paying Money); Subchapter I (Deposits And Depositaries). Current through Public Law 119-134, as published by the Office of the Law Revision Counsel. (a) The Secretary of the Treasury shall— (1) receive and keep public money; (2) take receipts for money paid out by the Secretary; (3) give receipts for money deposited in the Treasury; (4) endorse warrants for receipts.
